commentary: Benchmark indices show surface resilience reclaiming 23,000, yet market breadth remains narrow with a weak score of 36. Stan Weinstein's stage analysis warns that leadership cannot thrive when broad participation lags. In William O'Neil's discipline, a WEAK market gate dictates defensive caution and strict progressive exposure: even classic breakouts encounter heightened churn when institutional selling pressures the general tape. Jesse Livermore emphasized sitting tight rather than forcing trades in mixed environments. Exposure must be severely rationed, limited only to verified earnings accelerators trading at proper low-risk pivot buy points, with predefined stop losses enforced without compromise.
